newsitem.title: GERMANY: CSA expands flights, passenger capacity to Germany.
newsitem.headline: CSA expands flights, passenger capacity to Germany.

text.p: Czech airline CSA said it has increased seat capacity between Germany and the Czech Republic by 50 percent this summer.
Dusan Pavlasek, CSA passenger and cargo sales manager Germany, said the carrier has launched a daily Munich-Prague flight and added frequencies to Hamburg and Hanover from March 30.
This amounted to an extra 1,500 seats a week, or a 50 percent rise on the summer 1996 capacity of 3,000 seats, he told Reuters in an interview.
"We have increased flights for the business traveller since 90 percent of demand is for morning flights to Prague and evening flights back," he said.

CSA German passenger numbers rose about four percent to 130,000 last year, including one-third business travellers, but sales revenue increased nearly 20 percent thanks to higher prices and more business class sales, Pavlasek said.
But he added: "The market is stagnating and sales figures for the first few months of 1997 are all down."
From April 1, CSA flies daily except for Saturdays between Munich and Prague with an ATR-42 aircraft.
A code-share deal giving CSA blocked seats on the twice-daily Deutsche Lufthansa AG flights on the same route has been ended but could be revived later this summer, Pavlasek said.
Second daily flights have been added from Hamburg and Hanover to Prague, also with ATR-42 aircraft.
In all, CSA flies to seven German airports, including twice-daily Frankfurt-Prague flights with a Boeing 737-500. -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom. Tel +44 171 542 7706; Fax: 5017
